source.title: MaskTab: Scalable Masked Tabular Pretraining with Scaling Laws and Distillation for Industrial Classification
source.authors: Bo Zheng; Yudong Chen; Zihua Xiong; Shuai Fang; Peidong He; Yang Yang; Sheng Guo

page_placements.theme: Individual tasks and metrics can plateau or reverse with scale

record.file_problem: No apparent problem; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies scaling-study ideas to tabular classification and reports results in that new setting, but it does not test the language-model held-out-loss power laws or fit the same power-law form.
record.gate_note: The paper reports tabular OOT KS as unlabeled-data volume, feature count, and model parameter count vary. These are not language-model pretraining-loss measurements or fits of the power-law form in the claim versions. The paper also cites prior scaling-law work and says it follows Hoffmann et al.'s optimization protocol; cited results and the optimization-protocol reference are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs one-axis-at-a-time scaling sweeps for a tabular classifier: unlabeled data, feature count, and parameters. It reports only downstream OOT KS, with no held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit. Its results therefore cannot show whether any version's power-law, extrapolation, allocation, shape or fit claim holds. The record's 'discusses' and T3 pair is inconsistent, since T3 implies a test. I recode the tranche to T6. Citing Kaplan and Hoffmann, and borrowing Hoffmann's optimisation protocol, is not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is mostly right. The authors claim clear scaling trends, with performance improving predictably in unlabeled data, feature dimension and model capacity, and offering guidance for compute allocation. In the Limitations they concede the greedy one-axis study yields no formal joint scaling law. Their own Section 4.6 numbers show drops at the largest setting on every axis, which they call saturation, so 'predictably' is not backed by any fit.
record.recipe_differences: This is tabular classification pre-training evaluated by OOT AUC and KS, not language-model held-out cross-entropy. It varies unlabeled-data volume, feature count, and model parameters rather than fitting language-model loss laws or optimizing a parameter-token split under fixed compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported results vary with unlabeled-data volume, feature count, and parameter count; performance declines at the largest reported setting for each of these axes.

fits_no_version.finding: In tabular masked pretraining on CreditRisk, OOT KS peaks and then falls at the largest tested setting on each axis. Unlabeled data: 0.3594 at 20× vs 0.3480 at 40×. Features: 0.3754 at 2,000 vs 0.3653 at 2,500. Parameters: 0.4145 at 134M vs 0.4021 at 201M. Each result is from a single run with no uncertainty reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In industrial tabular pretraining, downstream classification metrics saturate or decline when any single scaling axis is increased while the others stay fixed, rather than following a monotone power law.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The scaling study is explicitly not exhaustive: it scales one dimension at a time and does not provide a formal joint scaling law. The reported sweep results have no uncertainty estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 plots additional intermediate settings for data volume, feature count, and model size, but the text does not state their exact values. They are not separately recorded because the supplied figure text does not provide extractable values.

untested.parts: All: no language-model pretraining loss and no power-law fit.
All: the MaskTab-S/M/L/XL family varies depth and width together with size, with no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Whether a power-law loss form holds in tabular pretraining: no loss curve is reported and no power law is fitted.
Downstream predictability for language models: only tabular KS is measured, with no fitted trend.
All: no exponent fitting or method comparison.

missing.what: Intermediate KS values for 0×, 5× and 10× unlabeled data, 1,000–1,500 features, and the S/M models (56M, 75M). These are plotted only, not stated in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses 'scaling law' loosely; it contains no functional fit. Its percentage gains are absolute KS points. The labeled-only baseline is about 0.340, close to Table 2's MaskTab-Base KS of 0.3398. Note that Table 2's Base was trained on labeled data only.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between model parameters and training tokens, and its trend with compute.
Architecture-shape effects on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether held-out pretraining loss follows the same power-law form in another modality or training regime.
Downstream task performance as a predictable function of language-model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model power-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting and setup choices.

relation.reason: The paper discusses established scaling laws and presents related tabular scaling sweeps without testing a defined claim version.

tranche.reason: The one-axis downstream KS sweeps establish trends and saturation, but test no power-law form, extrapolative prediction, compute-optimal allocation, architecture invariance, or fitted-law dependence. Downstream predictability is asserted rather than evaluated.

source_check.notes: The reported percentage gains should not be interpreted as established relative gains; 0.4145−0.3754 is 0.0391 KS. Section 4.6 gives XL as 201.32M parameters, while Table 7 lists 201.33M and identifies counts as non-embedding.
